TWIN4DEM · Netherlands case · Tweede Kamer and cabinet · 2008–2025

NL Agent Explorer

Everyone who held a seat in the Tweede Kamer or a cabinet post between 2008 and 2025: their offices, party, background, committees, connections, the bills they sponsored with the Raad van State's advice on them, and a yearly index of how their own plenary speech leans between executive discretion and checks on the executive.

Start here

This site describes the 674 people who sat in the Tweede Kamer or in a Dutch cabinet between 2008 and 2025, one profile per person, with everything traced back to public records.

  1. Pick a person from the list on the left, or search by name, party or group. Filters narrow the list to, say, ministers under Rutte III.
  2. Read the profile: offices over time, the stance index with its plain-language summary, background, committees, supporters, and the bills they sponsored with the Raad van State's advice.
  3. Follow the links: every co-signer, supporter and leader is clickable; the Connections tab shows who studied, sat and legislated with whom; Charts places every person in the party landscape and against their own party; Bills & Raad van State lets you search all 4,309 bills by topic and advice.
Try: · The stance index counts words; read how it is made before comparing people.
Click a person, or use ↑ ↓ and Enter. The sparkline is the yearly stance index.

Who is connected to whom, and through what. Type a name, choose what kind of connection you want to see, and read the picture from left to right: the person, what they share, and who they share it with.

Where they studied

Institutions recorded on Wikidata for the people on this site. Click one to see its alumni.

Six pictures that place people rather than parties: where they sit in the party landscape, how far they are from their own party, what happens to their speech when their party enters government, whose bills draw objections, and how the speech index compares with what experts say about their party. The selected person is ringed and named in every picture; click any dot to open that person.

Every bill (wetsvoorstel) deposited in the Tweede Kamer since 2008, with the subject categories the Kamer assigns to its dossier, the submitters linked to the people on this site, the final vote, and the Raad van State's opinion on the bill, classified from A (no remarks) to D (do not proceed).

Sources

Limits of the Dutch record

  • Districts. The Netherlands is one national constituency, so everything here is national.
  • Votes. Votes are recorded per party group; named roll-calls exist for 73 sessions.
  • Social media. Data-protection rules keep post text out of reach, so the stance index rests on plenary speech.
  • Judges. Raad van State opinions are signed collectively without dissents, and the ethics review rules out profiling individual judges; the court signal is per opinion and per year.
  • Courts and laws. The Raad van State advises before deposit, and the constitutionality of laws rests with parliament; the A to D class records the adviser's resistance.

How the tables connect

One person key links everything about a person; the party label links to the party layer; the dossier number links bills, topics, votes, Raad van State opinions and the flagged bills. The person layer and the act layer meet through the submitters of each bill.

Sources: OpenKamer, Tweede Kamer open data, Handelingen from the official publications repository, Raad van State advisory opinions, the Chapel Hill Expert Survey, Wikipedia and Wikidata. Data snapshot mid-2025. Built for the Netherlands case of TWIN4DEM.

NL Agent Explorer is an output of TWIN4DEM, Strengthening Democratic Resilience Through Digital Twins, a Horizon Europe project (grant agreement 101178061) coordinated by Erasmus University Rotterdam that builds digital twins of four European democracies to study executive aggrandisement. The Dutch case is one of them.
